distinctions_drawn: Literalist vs. structural parsing of predication
Participation as instance-universal vs. derivative-essential relation
explicit_definitions_given: SP: the Form of F is itself F in the same sense as particulars
NI: the Form is numerically distinct from any particular and any mediating entity
TMA: infinite regress generated by SP+NI+one-over-many

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: The text anticipates the objection that alternative solutions are anachronistic and responds by appealing to the trajectory of Plato's later dialogues and the dialectical purpose of the Parmenides.
objections_raised: Alternative solutions may sacrifice historical plausibility by reading later metaphysics into the early Theory of Forms.
Neutralizing the TMA may diminish the dialectical power of the Parmenides.

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: conceptual analysis, historical trajectory, textual interpretation

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Plato's Theory of Forms, self-predication, non-identity, infinite regress, participation

structural_organization.structure_type: recursive dialectical elaboration with sections: introduction, Vlastos's interpretation, TMA exposition, engine of regress, inconsistency, alternative solutions, historical plausibility, conclusion

summary_of_core_decisions: The text accepts Vlastos's diagnosis of inconsistency under a literalist reading but rejects the conclusion that Plato's ontology is inevitably inconsistent. It proposes reinterpretations of SP and NI that halt the regress while preserving the dualistic structure of the Forms.
